Summary of Pumping Test

A pumping test was carried out on the west side of the Po Shan slip
remedial works in ocorenole 21 (Figure Bl). Tne site of the test was on a
steep hillside of 26° average slope in completely decomposed volcanic
rock.

Tne results showed a delayed yield behaviour and consideraple
inhomogeneity of the ground. Despite this, a reasonaply reliable estimate
of transmissivity, and hence permeability, was obtained. However, the
value for specific yield is uncertain, as the test was affected py
rainfall after approximately 10.5 days of pumping. The mean value or
specific yield calculated is very low but, despite uncertainties, it is
unlikely to be less than half the actual average value. This reflects the
effect of boulders in reducing the pore space available for storage, and
the high water retention of the well-graded decomposed volcanic rock.

Average values of transmissivity, permeability, storativity and
specific yield are given in Table BI. Because multiple analysis
techniques on a number of boreholes were used to determine these values,
the standard deviation/mean value was calculated. These values, which are
shown in Table Bi, are probably realistic indications of the reliability
of the parameters, the results with a low standard deviation/mean value
Yatio being more reliable than those with a high value. No correlation
between boulder content above bedrock and permeability could be found, and
no allowance was made for flow to or from bedrock.

The drilling of the trial horizontal drains in the vicinity of the
pumping test is not expected to have had a significant influence on the
results obtained.

From the analysis, an effective borehole diameter of 400 mm was
calculated for a borehole of diameter 200 mn using oil well test
procedures.
